reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a widely debunked neuroscientific myth. Brain imaging technology such as fMRI and PET scans has established that humans use virtually every part of the brain, with almost all regions showing activity throughout the day. Furthermore, damage to even small areas of the brain typically causes significant deficits, which would not occur if 90% of the brain were dormant.
